_why_a_separate_file: This is one source's assertions, not a merged truth set. Keeping each source in its
own file is what makes arbitration possible: a claim can be attributed, scored, and
contradicted. Merging Elastic into shai_hulud_2026_08.json would destroy the
provenance that lets a source proven wrong start the next hunt already calibrated.
The hunt queries the union of all source files; it reports the arbitrated verdict set.

confirms: commit message 'chore: update config' authored claude@users.noreply.github.com
repo description marker 'Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again.'

npm preinstall hook as the primary execution trigger

_relationship_to_shai_hulud_2026_08.note: Silence is not denial. An indicator absent here is unclaimed by Elastic, not refuted by it, and stays in hunt scope on the other source's assertion.

ethereum.role: Live C2 address is read from chain at runtime with multiple RPC provider fallbacks, so domain blocking alone does not sever control.

dropper.behaviour: Detects platform and architecture, downloads Bun 1.3.13 from the official GitHub release page, executes the payload under Bun, then deletes the temporary Bun directory.

collector.behaviour: Heavily obfuscated credential harvester matching 300+ unique patterns.
collector.exfil: Credentials gzip-compressed, encrypted AES-256-GCM, key encrypted with RSA. Fallback channel is a public GitHub repository created under the compromised victim account.

execution_variants.note: Double-space variant Elastic uses in its own hunting query. A process-telemetry query matching the single-space form as a literal misses this. Match on the tokens, not the spacing.

propagation.note: Where a GitHub App token is stolen, the worm commits hooks to up to 50 branches per accessible repository. A hunt that inspects only the default branch will read a compromised repository as clean.

_dune_string_caveat: These are strings inside the payload, useful for identifying an unhashed or repacked
variant, and for spotting dead-drop repository names. They are ordinary English or
Dune-fiction words: 'navigator', 'mentat' and 'sandworm' will match unrelated code,
package names and file paths. Treat a match as a lead requiring a hash or a second
indicator, never as a detection on its own.

devops: npm tokens, with stated preference for those holding package write permission and bypass_2fa: true
_why_this_matters_here: The AI-tooling targets are new relative to prior Shai-Hulud reporting and they are
present on this estate: developer workstations running Claude Code and Cursor hold
exactly these credentials. Scoping credential-rotation to GitHub and npm tokens
would leave the set the collector was specifically built to take.

package_scope_claimed.note: Elastic names five root packages and does not enumerate the 400+. It therefore neither confirms nor refutes any specific version in the candidate set; registry packument evidence remains the only arbiter of which versions were malicious.

hunting_notes: Hunt the payload by hash, never by filename. regenerate-unicode-properties ships a legitimate General_Category/Math_Symbol.js, present in the Yarn cache on this very workstation at sha256 a59eed71ac12ea18eaa905caab8b2a6d83e4b51fd043f1d7830da5a943db1a52. A filename hunt returns it on every machine that ever installed a Babel or ESLint toolchain.

A folderOpen task in .vscode/tasks.json is not itself an indicator: this workstation has a legitimate one that launches Claude Code. The indicator is the task invoking node against a .mjs in the repository, or the file matching the known hook hash.
The RPC providers are the chokepoint, not the C2 domains, because the live address is resolved on chain at runtime.

npm >= 12 does not run preinstall hooks by default. Environments on npm 12 remain exposed through the IDE autostart chain, which requires no npm install at all, so a detection keyed on npm execution misses them entirely.
